Look up species in the FISHMORPH table

Source: R/species-finder.R
find_fishmorph_species.Rd

Tells, for each name supplied, whether the species is present in the FISHMORPH trait table, and if not, whether a close spelling or its genus is. This is the engine of the "Species finder" tab of launch_fishmorph_space().

Usage

find_fishmorph_species(
  species,
  reference = NULL,
  source = NULL,
  max_distance = 2,
  n_suggestions = 3
)

Arguments

species

Character vector of names to look up.

reference

The FISHMORPH table: a data frame with a Species column (and optionally Family, Order, IUCN and the nine trait columns), or the path to a semicolon-separated CSV. NULL (default) reads the table bundled with the package for source.

source

"segment" or "landmark", used only when reference is NULL. NULL follows get_fishmorph_source().

max_distance

Maximum edit distance (Levenshtein) for a "close" match. 0 disables approximate matching.

n_suggestions

Number of nearest names reported in suggestions.

Value

A data frame with one row per query and the columns query, query_clean, status, match (the FISHMORPH name retained), distance (edit distance to it), Family, Order, IUCN (of the match, or of the genus for "genus_only"), complete_traits (whether the matched species has all nine traits, i.e. is placed in the morphological space), n_genus (number of FISHMORPH species in the queried genus) and suggestions (the nearest names, with their edit distance in brackets; for a genus query, species of that genus; NA for an exact match).

Details

Names are first cleaned: underscores and repeated blanks become single spaces, authorities and subspecies are dropped (only the first two words are kept), the qualifiers cf. and aff. are removed, and sp./spp. turn the query into a genus query. Matching is case-insensitive.

The status column follows a ladder of certainty: "exact" (the binomial is in the table); "close" (no exact match but a name at most max_distance character edits away – typically a typo or a gender ending, to be checked by eye, never accepted blindly); "genus_only" (the species is absent but other species of its genus are present); "absent"; "invalid" (nothing usable after cleaning). A close match is not a synonymy check: use validate_species_names() to resolve names against FishBase.

See also

launch_fishmorph_space(), validate_species_names(), load_fishmorph_reference()

Examples

ref <- data.frame(
  Species = c("Salmo trutta", "Salmo salar", "Gobio gobio"),
  Family  = c("Salmonidae", "Salmonidae", "Gobionidae"),
  Order   = c("Salmoniformes", "Salmoniformes", "Cypriniformes"))
find_fishmorph_species(c("salmo_trutta", "Salmo truta", "Salmo marmoratus",
                         "Gobio sp.", "Esox lucius"), reference = ref)
#>              query      query_clean     status        match distance     Family
#> 1     salmo_trutta     Salmo trutta      exact Salmo trutta        0 Salmonidae
#> 2      Salmo truta      Salmo truta      close Salmo trutta        1 Salmonidae
#> 3 Salmo marmoratus Salmo marmoratus genus_only         <NA>       NA Salmonidae
#> 4        Gobio sp.            Gobio genus_only         <NA>       NA Gobionidae
#> 5      Esox lucius      Esox lucius     absent         <NA>       NA       <NA>
#>           Order IUCN complete_traits n_genus
#> 1 Salmoniformes <NA>              NA       2
#> 2 Salmoniformes <NA>              NA       2
#> 3 Salmoniformes <NA>              NA       2
#> 4 Cypriniformes <NA>              NA       1
#> 5          <NA> <NA>              NA       0
#>                                             suggestions
#> 1                                                  <NA>
#> 2    Salmo trutta [1]; Salmo salar [5]; Gobio gobio [9]
#> 3   Salmo salar [8]; Salmo trutta [8]; Gobio gobio [13]
#> 4                                           Gobio gobio
#> 5 Gobio gobio [10]; Salmo salar [11]; Salmo trutta [11]
